readmePreview: SQLite Source Repository This repository contains the complete source code for the SQLite database engine going back to 2000-05-29.

overview.summary: This is the canonical source tree for SQLite 3.54.0 (VERSION, manifest.uuid `c9b4695f...`) — a serverless, zero-configuration, public-domain SQL database engine implemented as a C library that compiles down to a single-file amalgamation (`sqlite3.c`). The tree is far more than the library: it also carries the `sqlite3` CLI shell (`src/shell.c.in`, ~14.9k lines with ~40 dot-commands), a dozen major extensions under `ext/` (FTS3/5, R-Tree/Geopoly, session/changesets, RBU, recover, intck, JNI bindings, a WASM/OPFS browser build), a TCL binding, and an unusually large test apparatus (1,195 `.test` scripts plus fuzzers). It is distinctive for being managed in Fossil rather than Git (this GitHub remote is a mirror), for refusing pull requests and agentic code on copyright grounds (AGENTS.md), for generating much of its own C (parser, opcodes, pragma table, keyword hash) from TCL/Lemon tooling, and for a testing culture where `make devtest` is the minimum bar before any check-in.

system_map.summary: The library is a layered stack inside one process: SQL text enters the tokenizer, goes through a Lemon-generated LALR(1) parser into a code generator, is optimized by the `where*.c` planner, and is executed as bytecode by the VDBE, which reaches storage through B-Tree → Pager → WAL → VFS. There is no daemon and no network boundary in the core; the only OS boundary is the `sqlite3_vfs` interface, implemented by `os_unix.c`, `os_win.c`, `os_kv.c` (key/value / browser localStorage) and `memdb.c`. Build is driven by autosetup (JimTCL-compatible), not GNU Autoconf, with `main.mk` holding the real rules and `Makefile.msc` mirroring them for MSVC. Deployment shape is a static/shared library plus the amalgamation tarball, the `sqlite3` CLI, and auxiliary binaries (`sqldiff`, `sqlite3_rsync`, `sqlite3_analyzer`, `testfixture`, `fuzzcheck`). Version control is Fossil; `manifest`, `manifest.uuid`, and `.fossil-settings/` are Fossil artifacts carried into the Git mirror.

claims.claim: The public C API is defined by the template `src/sqlite.h.in` (11,463 lines), which `tool/mksqlite3h.tcl` expands into the deliverable `sqlite3.h` by splicing in `VERSION` (3.54.0) and the SHA3 check-in id from `manifest.uuid`.

`openDatabase()` in `src/main.c:3388` is the single funnel for `sqlite3_open`, `sqlite3_open_v2` and `sqlite3_open16`: it calls `sqlite3_initialize()`, decides thread-safety from `SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX`/`FULLMUTEX` vs `sqlite3GlobalConfig.bFullMutex`, masks off internal-only open flags, allocates the `sqlite3` handle with `sqlite3MallocZero`, and enables lookaside plus `sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint`.

Compilation runs through `sqlite3LockAndPrepare()` (`src/prepare.c:854`), which takes `db->mutex`, calls `sqlite3BtreeEnterAll()` to hold every B-Tree mutex, and retries `sqlite3Prepare()` on `SQLITE_ERROR_RETRY` / `SQLITE_SCHEMA` up to `SQLITE_MAX_PREPARE_RETRY`.

The VDBE is the execution boundary: `sqlite3VdbeExec()` (`src/vdbe.c:902`) is one giant `for(pOp=&aOp[p->pc]; 1; pOp++)` dispatch loop over 190 `case OP_*` handlers, and `tool/mkopcodeh.tcl` scrapes those `case OP_` lines out of `vdbe.c` to assign opcode numbers.

Storage is layered strictly: `src/btree.c` (407KB, the largest file) exposes `sqlite3BtreeOpen/BeginTrans/Cursor/CommitPhaseOne/CommitPhaseTwo`, which sits on `src/pager.c`'s `sqlite3PagerOpen/Get/Write/CommitPhaseOne`, which in turn either journals or writes WAL frames via `src/wal.c`'s `sqlite3WalFrames`/`sqlite3WalCheckpoint`.

The OS boundary is a registry of `sqlite3_vfs` objects; `os_unix.c` registers up to 12 named VFSes (`unix`, `unix-none`, `unix-dotfile`, `unix-excl`, `unix-flock`, `unix-afp`, `unix-nfs`, `unix-proxy`, …) via a `UNIXVFS()` macro table at `src/os_unix.c:8497`, each pairing a locking style with an `IOMETHODS()`-generated `sqlite3_io_methods` vtable.

Alternative VFS backends ship in-tree: `src/memdb.c` registers a `memdb` VFS backing `sqlite3_serialize`/`sqlite3_deserialize`, and `src/os_kv.c` registers `kvvfs`, the key/value VFS used by the WASM/browser build.

The build entrypoint is `./configure`, a 4-line shell wrapper that execs autosetup; `auto.def` drives it via `sqlite-configure canonical`, where `--dev` implies `--all --debug`, disables the amalgamation, and sets `CFLAGS=-O0 -g`.

`main.mk` is the real makefile body (84KB): it defines `LIBOBJS0` (per-file objects) vs `LIBOBJS1 = sqlite3.o` (amalgamation) selected by `USE_AMALGAMATION`, and builds `sqlite3.c` by running `tool/mksqlite3c.tcl` over a generated `tsrc/` directory.

The CLI shell is generated, not compiled directly: `src/shell.c.in` uses `INCLUDE ../ext/...` directives (processed by `tool/mkshellc.tcl`) to inline ~25 extension source files — sha1/shathree, base64/base85, decimal, ieee754, series, regexp, fileio, completion, appendvfs, zipfile, sqlar, vfstrace, diskused, plus the `expert`, `intck`, `recover` and `qrf` libraries.

Auxiliary deliverables live in `tool/`: `sqldiff.c` (database diffing), `sqlite3_rsync.c` (rsync-like replication over SSH), `sqlite3_analyzer.c.in` (space analysis, paired with `tool/spaceanal.tcl`), `showdb.c`/`showwal.c`/`showjournal.c` (file-format forensics), and `lemon.c` (the parser generator itself).

A second, reduced build tree exists under `autoconf/` for the shipped amalgamation tarball (its own `auto.def`, `Makefile.in`, `Makefile.msc`, `Makefile.fallback`, plus a `tea/` TCL Extension Architecture build), and `tool/srctree-check.tcl` enforces that `autoconf/Makefile.msc` stays in sync with the top-level `Makefile.msc`.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing surface splits three ways: the C API in `sqlite.h.in`, the `sqlite3` CLI's dot-command language, and the loadable/compiled-in extension set. The CLI carries roughly 40 dot-commands covering schema inspection, import/export, archives, diagnostics, and integrity checking, plus 23 result-output modes now rendered by the new `ext/qrf` formatting library. Extensions add full-text search, spatial indexing, changeset/session replication, incremental update (RBU), corruption recovery, index recommendation, and a large `ext/misc/` grab-bag of 60 single-file functions and virtual tables. Configure-time feature flags (`--all` implies fts4, fts5, rtree, geopoly, session, dbpage, dbstat, carray) decide what lands in the amalgamation.

claims.claim: `do_meta_command()` (`src/shell.c.in:9947`) dispatches ~40 dot-commands including `.archive`, `.auth`, `.clone`, `.dump`, `.eqp`, `.expert`, `.explain`, `.filectrl`, `.fullschema`, `.import`, `.imposter`, `.intck`, `.iotrace`, `.load`, `.log`, `.mode`, `.open`, `.recover`, `.schema`, `.session`, `.stats`, `.vfsinfo`, `.vfslist`, `.vfsname` and `.wheretrace`.

The shell supports 23 output modes enumerated in the `aModeInfo[]` table at `src/shell.c.in:618` — ascii, box, c, column, count, csv, html, insert, jatom, jobject, json, line, list, markdown, off, psql, qbox, quote, split, table, tabs, tcl, www — each mapping to a QRF style plus separator/quoting/alignment settings.

Result formatting was factored out into a new library `ext/qrf/` (headed `2025-10-20`) whose `sqlite3_qrf_spec` struct carries style, escaping, quoting, word-wrap, column widths, alignment, screen width and `xRender`/`xWrite` callbacks; `shell_exec()` copies `pArg->mode.spec` into a local spec and installs `shellWriteQR` as the writer.

`open_db()` auto-registers a fixed extension set on every connection: sha/shathree, uint, stmtrand, decimal, base64, base85, regexp, ieee754, series, diskused, strdup, and (outside the WASM fiddle build) fileio and completion; zipfile and sqlar are added when `SQLITE_HAVE_ZLIB` is defined and safe mode is off.

The shell can open databases in four modes chosen by `deduceDatabaseType()` — normal file, append-VFS (`apndvfs`), ZIP archive (opened as `:memory:`), and hex-dump/deserialize — with `~/` expanded against `$HOME` when the literal path does not exist.

FTS5 is a full subsystem of 15 C files (`fts5_index.c`, `fts5_expr.c`, `fts5_storage.c`, `fts5_tokenize.c`, `fts5_vocab.c`, …) exposing a public `fts5_api` struct with `xCreateTokenizer`, `xCreateTokenizer_v2` and `xCreateFunction` for third-party tokenizers and auxiliary ranking functions.

The session extension implements changeset capture and replay: `sqlite3session_create`, `sqlite3session_attach`, `sqlite3session_changeset` (plus `_strm` streaming variants) and three generations of apply APIs — `sqlite3changeset_apply`, `_apply_v2`, `_apply_v3` — each with streaming counterparts.

Database recovery is a first-class feature: `ext/recover/sqlite3recover.c` plus `dbdata.c` implement the `.recover` dot-command by walking raw pages of a corrupt file, and are compiled into the CLI via `INCLUDE` directives.

The `.expert` command exposes `ext/expert/sqlite3expert.c`, which analyzes a query workload and recommends indexes; `shell_exec()` short-circuits to `expertHandleSQL()` whenever `pArg->expert.pExpert` is active.

`.intck` runs the incremental integrity-check library `ext/intck/sqlite3intck.c`, an alternative to `PRAGMA integrity_check` that can be run in bounded steps; it ships with its own six-file test suite.

`ext/misc/` holds 60 single-file extensions (series, regexp, fileio, decimal, base64/base85, uint, sha1/shathree, appendvfs, vfstrace, zipfile, sqlar, completion, memtrace, pcachetrace, diskused, …), most of which are excluded from the core amalgamation but compiled into the CLI.

In-memory serialization is a supported API path: `sqlite3_serialize()` (`src/memdb.c:750`) and `sqlite3_deserialize()` (`src/memdb.c:841`) move whole database images in and out of process memory, which is also what the shell's hex-db/deserialize open mode relies on.

data_flow.summary: Data enters as UTF-8 (or UTF-16, transcoded at the API edge) SQL text or as bound parameter values. `sqlite3RunParser` drives `sqlite3GetToken` token-by-token into the Lemon parser, which builds `Select`/`Expr`/`SrcList` trees inside a `Parse` object; the code generators turn those trees into a VDBE program of `Op` records. At run time the VDBE owns register memory (`Mem *aMem`) and cursors; reads and writes go through B-Tree cursors into the pager's page cache, and out to disk either as rollback-journal writes or WAL frame appends, always via `sqlite3_vfs` methods. Output leaves either as `sqlite3_column_*` values pulled from `p->pResultRow`, or — in the CLI — through QRF's `xWrite` callback into a `FILE*`. Schema itself round-trips through this same machinery: `sqlite3_schema` rows are re-parsed on load, which is why a schema cookie mismatch forces `sqlite3Reprepare`.

claims.claim: Text input is bounded at the tokenizer: `sqlite3RunParser` decrements `mxSqlLen` (initialized from `db->aLimit[SQLITE_LIMIT_SQL_LENGTH]`) by each token length and aborts with `SQLITE_TOOBIG` when it goes negative.

The tokenizer→parser handoff is a push loop: `sqlite3GetToken()` returns a token type and length, context-sensitive keywords are disambiguated by `analyzeWindowKeyword`/`analyzeOverKeyword`/`analyzeFilterKeyword`, and each token is pushed into the Lemon engine with `sqlite3Parser(pEngine, tokenType, pParse->sLastToken)`.
At end of input the parser is deliberately fed two synthetic tokens — `TK_SEMI` then `0` — so the grammar can reduce cleanly without a trailing semicolon in the source text.

SQL comments are conditionally dropped in the token stream rather than the grammar: `TK_COMMENT` is skipped only when `db->init.busy` (schema reparse) or `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_COMMENTS` is on, otherwise it falls through to an 'unrecognized token' error.

UTF-16 inputs are normalized at the boundary: `sqlite3_open16` converts the filename via `sqlite3ValueText(pVal, SQLITE_UTF8)` before calling `openDatabase`, and sets `SCHEMA_ENC`/`ENC` to `SQLITE_UTF16NATIVE` if the schema has not yet loaded.

Query plans are produced by `sqlite3WhereBegin()`, which chooses the nesting order of FROM-clause tables based on available indexes rather than written order, and emits the cursor-opening code that `sqlite3WhereEnd()` later closes.

`sqlite3Select()` is the funnel for all query code generation; it takes a `SelectDest` describing where rows go (`SRT_Output`, `SRT_Exists`, `SRT_Fifo`, `SRT_DistQueue`, …), so the same tree compiler serves top-level queries, subqueries, and recursive CTE queues.

Dirty-page flow at commit is branch-per-journal-mode inside `sqlite3PagerCommitPhaseOne`: in WAL mode it takes `sqlite3PcacheDirtyList()` and calls `pagerWalFrames()` (forcing page 1 into the list if empty, per ticket 2d1a5c67dfc2363e), otherwise it goes down the rollback-journal or batch-atomic-write path.

The pager state machine is explicit: `sqlite3PagerCommitPhaseOne` asserts the pager is in `PAGER_WRITER_LOCKED`, `WRITER_CACHEMOD`, `WRITER_DBMOD` or `PAGER_ERROR`, and returns early if it has not reached `PAGER_WRITER_CACHEMOD` (i.e. nothing was modified).

WAL readers snapshot through `sqlite3WalBeginReadTransaction` → `walTryBeginRead` → `walIndexReadHdr`, which reads the shared-memory wal-index header; the shm region itself is created by `unixOpenSharedMemory`/`unixLockSharedMemory` in the unix VFS.

In the CLI the output boundary is `shell_exec()`: it loops `sqlite3_prepare_v2` over the input buffer using `zLeftover` to advance through multi-statement text, and renders each result set through the QRF spec whose `xWrite` is `shellWriteQR`.

Interactive input is accumulated line-by-line in `process_input()`, which grows `zSql` by half-again increments, treats a leading `.` or `#` on a fresh buffer as a dot-command, and only executes when a semicolon is present *and* `sqlite3_complete(zSql)` agrees the statement is finished.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows carry most of the system's weight: library startup and connection open; the prepare/step/finalize query cycle including automatic recompilation on schema change; and the CLI's REPL loop from argv parsing through dot-command dispatch to statement execution. A fourth, the durability path, is worth tracing separately because commit behavior forks sharply between rollback-journal and WAL mode. Each trace below names the actual functions in call order as read from the sources.

claims.claim: Connection open trace: `sqlite3_open_v2` → `openDatabase` → `sqlite3_initialize` → mutex decision → flag masking → `sqlite3MallocZero(sizeof(sqlite3))` → `sqlite3MutexAlloc(SQLITE_MUTEX_RECURSIVE)` → `sqlite3_mutex_enter` → `db->eOpenState = SQLITE_STATE_BUSY` → … → `setupLookaside` → `sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint` → `opendb_out` label, which closes and nulls the handle on OOM or marks it `SQLITE_STATE_SICK` on other errors.

Prepare trace: `sqlite3_prepare_v2` → `sqlite3LockAndPrepare(db, zSql, nBytes, SQLITE_PREPARE_SAVESQL, 0, …)` → `sqlite3_mutex_enter(db->mutex)` → `sqlite3BtreeEnterAll(db)` → `sqlite3Prepare` (which memsets the `Parse` header/tail, links `sParse.pOuterParse`, and runs the parser) → retry loop → `sqlite3BtreeLeaveAll` → `sqlite3ApiExit` → `db->busyHandler.nBusy = 0`.

`SQLITE_PREPARE_PERSISTENT` changes allocation strategy mid-prepare: `sqlite3Prepare` increments `sParse.disableLookaside` and invokes `DisableLookaside` so long-lived statements do not pin lookaside slabs.

Step trace: `sqlite3_step` → `vdbeSafetyNotNull` → `sqlite3_mutex_enter` → inner `sqlite3Step` → (READY state) reset interrupt flag, bump `db->nVdbeActive`/`nVdbeWrite`/`nVdbeRead`, set `p->pc = 0`, move to `VDBE_RUN_STATE` → `sqlite3VdbeExec` (or `sqlite3VdbeList` when explaining) → on `SQLITE_DONE` with autocommit, `doWalCallbacks(db)`.

Auto-reset trace: when `sqlite3_step` is called on a statement already in `VDBE_HALT_STATE`, `sqlite3Step` calls `sqlite3_reset()` and `goto restart_step` — behavior introduced in 3.7.0, with `SQLITE_OMIT_AUTORESET` restoring the pre-3.6.23 `SQLITE_MISUSE` return.

Schema-change recovery trace: `sqlite3_step` loops while `sqlite3Step` returns `SQLITE_SCHEMA` (bounded by `SQLITE_MAX_SCHEMA_RETRY`), calling `sqlite3Reprepare(v)` → `sqlite3LockAndPrepare` on the saved SQL → `sqlite3VdbeSwap` → `sqlite3TransferBindings` → `sqlite3VdbeResetStepResult` → `sqlite3VdbeFinalize` of the throwaway VM, so bound parameters survive recompilation.

VDBE entry trace: `sqlite3VdbeExec` asserts `VDBE_RUN_STATE`, takes B-Tree mutexes via `sqlite3VdbeEnter` when `p->lockMask` is non-zero, computes `nProgressLimit` from `db->nProgressOps`, checks `db->u1.isInterrupted` (jumping to `abort_due_to_interrupt`), then enters the opcode loop incrementing `nVmStep` per instruction.

CLI startup trace: `main()` → `setvbuf(stderr,…,_IONBF)` → `isatty(0)`/`isatty(1)` to set `stdin_is_interactive`/`stdout_is_console` → `atexit(abnormalExit)` → optional `SQLITE_DEBUG_BREAK` debugger attach → `signal(SIGINT, interrupt_handler)`, `SIGTERM`/`SIGHUP` → `sqlite3_sourceid()` vs `SQLITE_SOURCE_ID` mismatch check that exits 1.

`main_init()` runs before any SQLite use and configures the library globally: `sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG, shellLog, p)`, `verify_uninitialized()`, `sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_URI, 1)` and `sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_MULTITHREAD)` — so the CLI runs in multithread (not serialized) mode with URI filenames enabled.

REPL trace: `process_input` → `one_input_line` → whitespace/`.`/`#` classification → `do_meta_command` for dot-commands (return code 2 means exit) → otherwise append to `zSql` → `sqlite3_complete` gate → `runOneSqlLine` → `shell_exec` → `sqlite3_prepare_v2`/step loop → QRF render.

Startup also sources `~/.sqliterc` through the same `process_input` path unless `-noinit` was given, and exits 1 on error when `bail_on_error` is set — meaning the rc file is executed with full dot-command privileges before the user's first keystroke.

Lazy-open trace: the shell does not open a database at startup; every dot-command that needs one calls `open_db(p, 0)` first (over 25 call sites), which is what makes `sqlite3` usable with no arguments and then `.open` later.

testing_signals.summary: Testing is TCL-first: 1,195 `.test` scripts in `test/` are executed by `testfixture`, an augmented tclsh built from `src/tclsqlite.c` plus 44 `src/test*.c` harness modules that expose internals (malloc fault injection, VFS shims, thread control, syscall interception) to TCL. `test/testrunner.tcl` parallelizes across cores and drives named suites and permutations; `permutations.test` defines 58 test_suite configurations. `make devtest` — the developers' minimum pre-check-in bar — chains `srctree-check` (generated files up to date) and `sourcetest` before running `testrunner.tcl mdevtest`. Fuzzing is a separate, substantial tier: `fuzzcheck` replays fuzzer corpora stored as SQLite databases, and `ossfuzz.c` is the OSS-Fuzz entry point. No CI configuration lives in the repo; extension suites are colocated with their extensions.

claims.claim: The test corpus is 1,195 `.test` TCL scripts under `test/`, run by the `testfixture` binary built from `$(TESTFIXTURE_SRC)`; `make smoketest` runs just `./testfixture test/main.test` as the fast sanity check.

`make devtest` depends on `srctree-check` and `sourcetest`, then runs `test/testrunner.tcl mdevtest`; `test`, `quicktest` and the legacy `fulltest`/`alltest`/`soaktest` targets are aliases onto `devtest` or `releasetest`.

`tool/srctree-check.tcl` is a guard against stale generated artifacts: it regenerates `autoconf/Makefile.msc` via `tool/mkmsvcmin.tcl` and diffs it, and checks `VERSION` against `autoconf/tea/configure.ac`, exiting non-zero with a suggested fix command.

`test/testrunner.tcl` bootstraps its own interpreter: `find_interpreter` tries `package require sqlite3`, falls back to sourcing a local `pkgIndex.tcl`, then to re-execing under `./testfixture`, and finally offers to build the TCL extension — which is why `make tclextension-install` is recommended before testing.
The runner estimates work per job class with weights `tcl=1`, `fuzz=22`, `bld=66`, `make=102` (optionally overridden by `test/testrunner_estwork.tcl`) so parallel scheduling packs long builds first.

`test/testrunner_data.tcl` is the declarative test matrix: `trd_builds`, `trd_configs`, `trd_extras`, `trd_all_configs`, `trd_fuzztest_data` and `trd_buildscript` define per-platform build configurations and which suites each one runs, mirroring the old `all.test`.

`test/permutations.test` defines 58 `test_suite` permutations, letting the same `.test` files be re-run under different pragma/compile configurations (this is also what `make valgrindtest` invokes with the `valgrind` permutation).

44 `src/test*.c` modules expose internals to TCL for white-box testing, including `test_malloc.c` (allocation fault injection), `test_vfs.c`/`test_devsym.c`/`test_demovfs.c` (VFS simulation), `test_journal.c`, `test_syscall.c` (syscall interception), `test_thread.c`, `test_mutex.c` and `test_pcache.c`.

`test/fuzzcheck.c` replays fuzzer output stored in SQLite databases with `db(dbid, dbcontent)` and `xsql(sqlid, sqltext)` tables, looking only for crashes, assertion faults and leaks — it explicitly does not verify output; eight `fuzzdata*.db` corpora ship in-tree.

`test/ossfuzz.c` is the Google OSS-Fuzz `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` harness with debug flags (`FUZZ_SQL_TRACE`, `FUZZ_SHOW_MAX_DELAY`, `FUZZ_SHOW_ERRORS`) that can be driven interactively through `test/ossshell.c`.

Additional specialized fuzzers exist for distinct attack surfaces: `test/dbfuzz.c` and `test/dbfuzz2.c` (database file images), `test/sessionfuzz.c` (changeset blobs), `test/optfuzz.c` (query optimizer equivalence), and `test/fuzzinvariants.c` (result invariants).

Extension test suites live beside their extensions rather than in `test/`: 149 files under `ext/fts5/test`, 44 `.test` files in `ext/session/`, 43 in `ext/rbu/`, 27 in `ext/rtree/`, 15 in `ext/recover/`, and 5 in `ext/intck/`.

risk_map.summary: The core library is one of the most heavily tested C codebases in existence, so the interesting risk is not 'is this correct' but 'where does trust boundary crossing happen'. The sharpest edges are: the CLI, which by design shells out and touches the filesystem; `sqlite3_load_extension`, which `dlopen`s attacker-suppliable paths; the schema itself, which is executable input (the `trusted-schema`/`defensive` model exists precisely because of this); and `sqlite3_rsync`, which `fork`/`execl`s a shell. Structurally, the blast radius is concentrated in a handful of enormous files — `btree.c`, `select.c`, `vdbe.c`, `pager.c`, `where.c` are each 300–400KB — and in generated-file drift, which `srctree-check` only partially guards. Note that AGENTS.md explicitly states the project does not accept agentic code, which is itself a process constraint on any change made here.

claims.claim: The shell has an explicit unsafe-operation surface gated only by `bSafeMode`: `failIfSafeMode()` guards `.archive`, `.cd`, `.clone`, `.import`, `.load`, `.read`, `.restore` and shell-out, and `safeModeAuth()` blocks the functions `edit`, `fts3_tokenizer`, `load_extension`, `readfile`, `realpath`, `writefile`, `zipfile`, `zipfile_cds` plus `ATTACH`.

Safe mode is implemented as an authorizer callback, so it is only active when `SQLITE_OMIT_AUTHORIZATION` is not defined — the whole `safeModeAuth`/`shellAuth` block is inside `#ifndef SQLITE_OMIT_AUTHORIZATION`, meaning a build without the authorizer silently loses these protections.

The CLI calls `system()` directly in at least two places (the `edit()` SQL function at `src/shell.c.in:2505` and the `.shell`/`.system` dot-command at `:6045`) and `sqlite3_popen()` in three more (`.import` from a pipe, output redirection to a pipe, and `.read` from a pipe), all constructing command strings from user input.

`open_db()` unconditionally calls `sqlite3_enable_load_extension(p->db, 1)` on every CLI connection, re-enabling a capability the library deliberately disables by default; the `.load` dot-command is then only stopped by safe mode.

`sqlite3LoadExtension()` passes the caller-supplied path to `sqlite3OsDlOpen` and, on failure, retries with platform suffixes (`.so`/`.dylib`/`.dll`) appended — the only guards are the `SQLITE_LoadExtension` flag, a zero-length-name rejection (to prevent linking the running binary), and a `SQLITE_MAX_PATHLEN` cap added because some `dlopen()` implementations segfault on oversize names.

The schema is an execution surface: `doc/trusted-schema.md` documents that an attacker who modifies a database's schema (swapping a table for a view, adding triggers, CHECK constraints, generated columns or index expressions) can get code to run in a high-privilege reader's process, which is why functions carry Innocuous/Normal/Direct-Only risk levels and `TRUSTED_SCHEMA` defaults to *on* for backwards compatibility.

The CLI ties both hardening knobs to one flag: `open_db` sets `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_TRUSTED_SCHEMA` to the value of `--unsafe-testing` and `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DEFENSIVE` to its inverse, so enabling testing mode disables defensive mode in the same breath.

`ext/misc/fileio.c` provides `readfile()`/`writefile()` SQL functions that do arbitrary filesystem I/O; they are registered with `SQLITE_DIRECTONLY` (blocking use from triggers/views/schema) but are plain callable functions from top-level SQL, and the shell compiles them in by default.

`tool/sqlite3_rsync.c` embeds a `popen2()` implementation copied from Fossil that `fork()`s and `execl()`s either the command directly or `/bin/sh -c zCmd`, building the command from a user-supplied `--ssh` program name and a `USER@HOST:PATH` argument — a shell-injection-shaped surface in a network-facing tool.

Blast radius is concentrated in five files that dominate the tree: `btree.c` (408KB), `select.c` (337KB), `vdbe.c` (325KB), `pager.c` (305KB), `where.c` (298KB) — any edit in these touches the hot path for essentially every query.

Generated files are a standing hazard: `sqlite3.h`, `parse.c`/`parse.h`, `opcodes.h`/`opcodes.c`, `keywordhash.h`, `pragma.h` and `sqlite3.c` must never be hand-edited, and `tool/srctree-check.tcl` only verifies two things (Makefile.msc sync and VERSION vs tea/configure.ac) — it does not detect a hand-edited `pragma.h` or `parse.c`.

Opcode numbering is implicitly coupled to source formatting: `tool/mkopcodeh.tcl` derives opcode numbers by scanning `src/vdbe.c` for lines beginning with `case OP_`, so a reformatting or reordering of those 190 case labels silently renumbers the bytecode.

extension_points.summary: SQLite is built almost entirely out of registries, which is why it has such a large third-party ecosystem. At the C level there are seven pluggable interfaces: VFS, virtual-table modules, scalar/aggregate/window functions, collations, page cache, memory allocator, and mutex implementation — plus auto-extensions that fire on every new connection. Above that, FTS5 has its own nested registry for tokenizers and ranking functions. On the source-tree side, the extension points are code generators: adding a PRAGMA means editing `tool/mkpragmatab.tcl`, adding an opcode means adding a `case OP_` in `vdbe.c`, adding grammar means editing `parse.y`, and adding a CLI dot-command means editing the `do_meta_command` chain in `shell.c.in`.

claims.claim: VFS registry: `sqlite3_vfs_register()`/`sqlite3_vfs_unregister()`/`sqlite3_vfs_find()` form the OS-abstraction plug point, used in-tree by `memdb.c` (the `memdb` VFS) and `os_kv.c` (`kvvfs`), and exported to loadable extensions through the `sqlite3_api_routines` thunk in `loadext.c`.

Virtual-table registry: `sqlite3_create_module()` and `sqlite3_create_module_v2()` in `src/vtab.c:108-130` register a `sqlite3_module` vtable implementation; this is how `series`, `zipfile`, `dbstat`, `dbpage`, FTS and R-Tree all attach.

Function registry: built-ins are installed by `sqlite3RegisterBuiltinFunctions()` (`src/func.c:3368`) from a static `FUNCTION(...)` macro table, and the same mechanism is exposed publicly as `sqlite3_create_function*` — extensions like `decimal.c`, `base85.c` and `shathree.c` use it exclusively.

Collation registry: `createCollation()` (`src/main.c:2907`) backs `sqlite3_create_collation*`; SQLite seeds four built-ins — BINARY in UTF8/UTF16BE/UTF16LE, plus NOCASE and RTRIM — at connection open.

Auto-extension registry: `sqlite3_auto_extension()` appends to the process-global `sqlite3Autoext` list guarded by `SQLITE_MUTEX_STATIC_MAIN`, and `sqlite3AutoLoadExtensions()` replays it on every new connection.

Loadable-extension ABI: `sqlite3LoadExtension` looks for `sqlite3_extension_init`, and if absent derives a name of the form `sqlite3_X_init` from the filename between the last `/` and the first `.`, lowercasing alphabetic characters — this is the convention every `ext/misc/*.c` file follows.

FTS5 exposes a second-level registry through `fts5_api`: `xCreateTokenizer`, `xCreateTokenizer_v2` (for custom text segmentation) and `xCreateFunction` (for auxiliary/ranking functions receiving an `Fts5ExtensionApi`).

Pluggable subsystem hooks are set through `sqlite3_config()` (`src/main.c:443`), which accepts `SQLITE_CONFIG_MALLOC`, `SQLITE_CONFIG_PAGECACHE`, `SQLITE_CONFIG_MUTEX`, `SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG`, `SQLITE_CONFIG_URI` and threading modes — the CLI itself uses the LOG, URI and MULTITHREAD forms.

PRAGMA extension point: new pragmas are declared as `NAME:`/`TYPE:`/`ARG:`/`IF:` records in the `pragma_def` block of `tool/mkpragmatab.tcl`, which regenerates `pragma.h`; the matching `case PragTyp_XXXXX:` is then added in `src/pragma.c`.

Grammar extension point: SQL syntax changes go in `src/parse.y` (2,169 lines), compiled by the in-tree Lemon generator `tool/lemon.c` against the `tool/lempar.c` template — never by editing `parse.c`.

Shell extension point: `src/shell.c.in` supports an `SQLITE_SHELL_EXTFUNCS` preprocessing hook in `open_db()` for downstream builds to register their own functions, alongside the `INCLUDE ../ext/...` mechanism processed by `tool/mkshellc.tcl`.

Authorizer hook: `sqlite3_set_authorizer()` (`src/auth.c:70`) installs a callback consulted by `sqlite3AuthCheck`/`sqlite3AuthRead` at code-generation time — `sqlite3Select` calls `sqlite3AuthCheck(pParse, SQLITE_SELECT, …)` before compiling any query — which is the hook the shell's `.auth` and safe mode both build on.

agent_handoff.summary: The hard constraints here are unusual and worth internalizing before touching anything: this is public-domain C with no license headers ever added, it is developed in Fossil (the Git remote is a mirror with different check-in names), and AGENTS.md states outright that the project does not accept agentic code — agentic *bug reports with reproducible test cases* are welcome, and patches are accepted only as proof-of-concept documentation. Practically, that means the safe posture is: read, reproduce, write a `.test` case, and propose rather than land. When editing is in scope, the rules are C89/C99 only, `sqlite3Malloc` family for all allocation, `i64`/`u32`/`u64` for width-sensitive values, `SQLITE_OK`/`SQLITE_*` return codes, liberal `assert` with `ALWAYS`/`NEVER` for compiler-opaque invariants, and never touching a generated file. Always run at least `make devtest` after any `src/` change.

claims.claim: Read first, in this order: `AGENTS.md` (project constraints and generated-file table), `README.md` (source tree map and build instructions), `src/sqliteInt.h` (6,031 lines — the master internal header), and `src/sqlite.h.in` (the public API template and the source of the API docs).

Never add a copyright or license header: every file carries the intentional 'May you do good and not evil' blessing comment instead, and adding a header would jeopardize the public-domain status the project depends on.

Do not hand-edit generated files: `sqlite3.h` (from `tool/mksqlite3h.tcl`), `parse.c`/`parse.h` (lemon on `src/parse.y`), `opcodes.h`/`opcodes.c` (`mkopcodeh.tcl`/`mkopcodec.tcl`), `keywordhash.h` (`tool/mkkeywordhash.c`), `pragma.h` (`tool/mkpragmatab.tcl`), `sqlite3.c` (`tool/mksqlite3c.tcl`).

Build for development with `./configure --dev`, which `auto.def` translates into `--all --debug`, amalgamation *off* (so each `src/*.c` compiles separately and errors point at real files), and `CFLAGS=-O0 -g`.

The configure script is autosetup, not GNU Autoconf, and must stay JimTCL-compatible — `autosetup/jimsh0.c` is bundled so the tree can configure without a system tclsh. Project-specific procs are prefixed `sqlite-` (in `autosetup/sqlite-config.tcl`), generic ones `proj-` (in `autosetup/proj.tcl`).

Tests need TCL: install `tcl-dev`, run `make tclextension-install` before `make devtest`, and note that `testrunner.tcl` will try to re-exec itself under `./testfixture` if `package require sqlite3` fails.

Minimum test bar for any `src/` change is `make devtest` (`srctree-check` + `sourcetest` + `testrunner.tcl mdevtest`); targeted runs use `./testfixture test/<file>.test` or `test/testrunner.tcl fts5%` pattern matching, and failures are found with `grep '!' testrunner.log`.

Coding conventions to match: C89/C99 only (no C++/VLAs), all allocation through `sqlite3Malloc`/`sqlite3MallocZero`/`sqlite3_malloc64` rather than raw `malloc`, `i64`/`u32`/`u64` instead of bare `long`/`int` for values that can exceed 2G, `SQLITE_OK`-style return codes with `db->mallocFailed` for deferred OOM detection.

`assert()` is used as executable documentation throughout and is expected in new code; use `ALWAYS(x)`/`NEVER(x)` for conditions the compiler cannot prove — e.g. `ALWAYS(cnt<=SQLITE_MAX_PREPARE_RETRY)` in the prepare retry loop and `NEVER(pPager->errCode)` in commit.

Requirement-traceability comments matter: `EVIDENCE-OF: R-#####-#####` markers in the sources tie code to numbered statements in the external documentation (e.g. in `sqlite3_prepare_v2`/`_v3`), and `testcase()` markers mark branches the test suite is expected to cover — preserve both when editing.

Match the file's existing idiom: this codebase uses two-space indentation, `if( cond ){` spacing with no space after `if`, `/* ... */` block comments only, and `**` comment continuation banners — deviating is immediately visible in diffs.

Safe edit boundaries: `ext/misc/*.c` single-file extensions and `test/*.test` scripts are the lowest-risk places to add code; `src/btree.c`, `src/pager.c`, `src/wal.c`, `src/vdbe.c` and `src/where.c` are the highest-risk and should not be touched without a reproducing test.
